intro: The most common reason homeowners in LowerLilyham enquire about wet room installation is accessibility — either planning ahead for later life, or adapting a bathroom after a family member's mobility has changed. That said, plenty of people here simply want a sleek, modern shower space without the hassle of a tray or screen. Either way, a properly installed wet room is a genuine long-term investment, and in LowerLilyham the work typically runs between £6,500 and £12,000 depending on the size, spec, and condition of what's already there. Get it right and you've got a space that's practical, adds value, and lasts decades. Get it wrong and you're dealing with damp, leaks, and expensive remedial work.
localContext: LowerLilyham has a real mix of property types, and that mix matters when it comes to wet room installation. Edwardian semis — common in the older residential streets — tend to have solid timber floor joists that need careful assessment before any wet room work begins. The floors in these homes can flex slightly over time, which puts stress on tanking membranes if they haven't been applied properly. Post-war estate homes, which make up a large portion of LowerLilyham's housing stock, often have concrete ground floors that are actually ideal for wet room conversion, though the bathroom sizes can be compact. Modern developments are generally more straightforward structurally, but may have en-suite spaces that are tight on drainage fall. On top of all this, LowerLilyham sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale build-up on screens, tiles, and shower fittings is a real consideration — experienced local installers will often recommend a water softener or at least limescale-resistant fittings as part of the overall package.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation in LowerLilyham typically follows a clear sequence of work, and understanding what's involved helps you plan realistically. The process begins with a site survey — a decent installer will assess your existing floor structure, check the drainage position and fall possibilities, and discuss waterproofing strategy before any quote is finalised. Once you've agreed on a design and materials, the first physical stage is stripping out the existing bathroom: removing the old suite, tiles, and flooring down to the substrate. From there, the floor is prepared and graded to create the correct fall toward the drain — usually around 1.5% — so water runs away cleanly without pooling. This is one of the most technically demanding parts of the job. After the sub-floor work, the entire wet zone is tanked using a waterproof membrane system applied to both floor and walls. This is the most critical stage; any shortcuts here will cause problems down the line. Tiling follows once the tanking has cured properly — typically 24 to 48 hours depending on the system used. Your chosen tiles, drain cover, shower fixture, and glass screen (if specified) are then fitted and sealed. Finally, sanitaryware is reinstalled and all plumbing connections are checked and tested. Most LowerLilyham wet room installations take between five and eight working days from strip-out to completion.
pricing: In LowerLilyham, a straightforward wet room conversion in a standard bathroom — including tanking, tiling with mid-range tiles, a linear drain, and a thermostatic shower — typically costs between £6,500 and £8,500. Larger bathrooms, premium tile choices, underfloor heating, or structural floor work in older Edwardian properties can push the total toward £10,000 to £12,000. If you're converting an en-suite in a modern development where space is limited and drainage options are restricted, expect to pay a premium for the additional planning and drainage engineering involved. Materials generally account for around 40–50% of the total cost. Always get three itemised quotes and be cautious of anything significantly below the local going rate — undercutting often means corners are being cut on waterproofing.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who regularly works in LowerLilyham makes a practical difference on a job like this. Local installers will know the typical floor construction in Edwardian semis and post-war estates here, understand which suppliers are reliable for materials in West Sussex, and can often visit for a survey quickly rather than weeks away. They're also easier to hold to account if something needs addressing after completion. Word-of-mouth matters in a mid-sized town like LowerLilyham — reputable tradespeople here rely on local reputation, which tends to focus the mind on doing the job properly first time.

faqs.q: Is my Edwardian semi in LowerLilyham suitable for a wet room?
faqs.a: Most Edwardian semis in LowerLilyham can be converted, but the timber joist floors require careful assessment first. An experienced installer will check for flex, may recommend strengthening the sub-floor, and will use a high-quality tanking system designed to handle slight movement. It's absolutely achievable — it just needs more preparation than a concrete floor property.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in LowerLilyham?
faqs.a: Most jobs in LowerLilyham take between five and eight working days, assuming no major structural surprises. Older properties occasionally reveal issues once the floor is stripped back — like damaged joists or outdated pipework — that add time. A good installer will flag potential risks at survey stage so you're not caught off guard mid-project.

faqs.q: Does hard water in LowerLilyham cause problems with wet rooms?
faqs.a: LowerLilyham's moderately hard water does mean limescale will build up on tiles, screens, and shower fittings faster than in soft water areas. Using a quality thermostatic shower with limescale-resistant internals helps, as does sealing grout properly and keeping on top of cleaning. Some homeowners in the area add an inline scale inhibitor to the shower supply — worth discussing with your installer.

faqs.q: Will a wet room add value to my LowerLilyham home?
faqs.a: A well-installed wet room generally adds value, particularly in a mid-to-larger property where buyers expect a quality bathroom. In LowerLilyham's housing market, a professionally finished wet room in an Edwardian semi or post-war home is seen as a genuine upgrade. Poor installation, however, can actually deter buyers — so the quality of the work matters as much as having one at all.
